ideas.description: Combine two near-misses: E084's bs-1024 32 px phase (+0.18 pp scored, +0.11 pp off-seed, +2.5% time) pays for the first fractional 32 px trim on a Muon base. Base: E084 code (3e30852, samples-indexed _fit, bs 1536 at 16/24 px, bs 1024 at 32 px) with E086's pinned staging buffer ported unchanged. The staging change is math-neutral and was confirmed bit-identical in E086/E087. Change only the length of the 32 px phase, from 4 to 3.75 epochs: 2@16 + 1.25@24 + 3.75@32 px (7.0 ep). The switch is indexed by samples seen. LR warmup/decay, the floor-hold, the final-EMA window, the lookahead stop and the renorm cadence are rescaled by samples, exactly as E084 did. All shapes are already warmed up in build. Precondition, untimed: log the source hash and a diff against 3e30852 plus 749bdce, so the run joins the right family (H4.2.4). Decide with an untimed off-seed run on seeds 3-10 plus two scored runs.
ideas.expected: Time about 4.44-4.50 s, which is -1.5 to -2.7% against the tip's 4.565 s. E084 is ~4.68 s after the pinned-staging saving, and 0.25 epoch at 32 px with bs 1024 costs ~0.22 s. Two-run scored pool 0.7540-0.7550 and off-seed 0.7526-0.7538, i.e. -0.05 to -0.15 pp against E084. Even after the trim, the 32 px phase keeps ~45 more steps than the tip. Bank it as the new tip if the pool is >=0.7537, the off-seed mean is >=0.7525 and time is <=4.50 s. A loss of >=0.25 pp against E084 means the 32 px phase is binding even with more steps, so H2.10.5 is refuted for whole-phase trims.

ideas.description: Equal-time sibling of the bs-1024 32 px trim idea, on the same base: E084 code plus the E086 pinned staging. Step 1, untimed: measure the compiled cost of a 28 px epoch at bs 1024 against a 32 px epoch at bs 1024 (2 epochs each, static shapes). If the ratio is >0.85x, drop the idea without a scored run. Step 2: replace the first 1.25 epochs of the 32 px phase with 28 px, using the same operator (flip + translate-2 at 32 px, then antialiased bilinear to 28 px; maps 27/13/6/3, max(dim).values pool). The schedule is 2@16 + 1.25@24 + 1.25@28 + 2.75@32 px. Samples seen are unchanged, so the step count is unchanged and LR/EMA/tail/renorm are untouched. Compile the bs-1024 28 px shape as a static graph and warm it up in build. Decide with an off-seed run on seeds 3-10 plus two scored runs, and compare against the trim arm.
ideas.expected: 28 px epoch cost about 0.76-0.82x of a 32 px epoch. Time about 4.43-4.48 s (-2 to -3% against the tip), about equal to the trim arm. Accuracy -0.03 to -0.12 pp against the E084 pool, i.e. a scored pool of ~0.7543-0.7552 and off-seed ~0.7530-0.7538. H10's corollary predicts this beats the trim arm by >=0.05 pp at equal time, because it keeps every update. If it is no better than the trim arm, step count is not the currency in the tail, and resolution substitution is closed.

ideas.description: Base: the current tip (E086 code 749bdce: E070 schedule, Fable tail, pinned staging). Remove the SGD-era lookahead-EMA entirely, so the net trains on its own weights throughout. Drop its buffers and its foreach kernels from build and from the step loop. Keep the floor-hold, the final 8-step EMA (0.3 lerp every 4 steps), eval on the EMA weights and the BN buffers copied from the net. Change nothing else. Decide with an untimed off-seed run on seeds 3-10 against the tip's 0.7530, plus two scored runs; read the per-trial train-time logs.
ideas.expected: Time -0.3 to -1% (about 4.52-4.55 s), from removing the lookahead's per-step weight traffic about every 3 steps. Accuracy: off-seed within -0.05 pp of 0.7530 or better, and a scored pool of ~0.7525-0.7545. Bank it if both scored runs are faster than 4.561 s and the off-seed delta is >= -0.05 pp. If the off-seed loss is >=0.15 pp, lookahead still carries real smoothing under Muon at ~240 steps, and the line closes.

ideas.description: Base: the tip (E086 code). Precondition, free: log the current whiten_bias_epochs value in step terms. Then verify, in an untimed compiled-graph dump, that the steps after the detach have no stem dgrad or bias-reduction kernels. This was the H2.15.1 premise, and code reading says it is already present. Change only the freeze point. Train the whitening bias for the first 0.2 epoch (~7 steps at bs 1536), with its own LR tensor decaying linearly to 0 over that window (hiverge), then switch to the existing whiten_bias_grad=False graph for the rest of training. Both graph variants already exist and are warmed up for 16 px; the 24/32 px shapes need only the detached variant. Decide with an off-seed run on seeds 3-10 plus two scored runs.
ideas.expected: Time -0.3 to -0.7% (about 4.535-4.55 s). E061 saved ~0.3% by moving the freeze from 37.5% to 20% of steps, and this removes the remaining ~17% of steps that train the bias, all inside the cheap 16 px phase. Accuracy: off-seed within 0.1 pp of 0.7530 and a scored pool of 0.7525-0.7545. If the off-seed drop is >=0.15 pp, the 64x-LR bias needs more than 7 steps on CIFAR-100, so keep the current point. If the time drop is <0.2% over two runs, the whitening-bias lever is exhausted.

ideas.description: Instrument calibration, with no recipe change. Rerun the unchanged tip (E086 code) on seeds 3-10 in at least 3 fresh processes through the benchmark's trial code. Each process rebuilds, so cuDNN benchmark picks are resampled. Continue until there are >=2 off-seed samples that are not bit-identical. Log the per-seed final-weight checksums (H4.4.1) and the cuDNN conv kernel names per (layer, shape) (H4.5.1). Report the sd of the 8-seed off-seed mean across the non-identical samples, and check whether the run means cluster by algorithm set. For the scored row, rerun the tip once; it adds a non-bit-identical tip sample if one occurs.
ideas.expected: Scored row ~4.56 s, accuracy 0.752-0.755. Prediction: the sd of the off-seed mean across divergent reruns is 0.07-0.15 pp, so a paired off-seed A/B has SE ~0.1-0.2 pp, and the past verdicts at |d|<=0.18 (E077/E078/E079/E081/E084) are each <1.5 SE. If the sd is <0.05 pp, those verdicts stand and off-seed alone can decide future ideas. Every queued idea's pass bar gets re-scaled from this number.

ideas.description: Ablation of E084's EMA-window confound. Base: E084 code plus the E086 pinned staging. Pin the final-EMA window and the lookahead stop to the tip's step counts (the last 8 steps, indexed from the end) instead of to equal sample counts, which gave ~12 steps at bs 1024. Change nothing else. Run one scored run and an off-seed run on seeds 3-10, compared against E084's off-seed 0.7541 and the tip's 0.7530. If the result is >= E084, use this window in the 32 px trim and 28 px arms that follow.
ideas.expected: Time equal to E084 within ±0.5% (~4.68 s). If update count is the mechanism, off-seed is 0.7538-0.7545 (within 0.05 pp of E084, gain >=+0.08 pp over the tip). If the gain falls to <=+0.03 pp against the tip, E084's effect came from the ~12-step window rather than the extra updates. In that case H2.11.3 is refuted as an update-count lever, and the trim arm built on E084 loses its funding rationale.

ideas.description: Placement test for update count. Base: the tip (E086 code), with the samples-indexed _fit from E084. Run bs 1024 in the 16 and 24 px phases only (~+53 steps), and keep the 32 px phase and the whole tail at bs 1536, so the final-EMA window stays at 8 steps. Index LR warmup/decay by samples, scale the SGD groups per phase by the kilostep rule, and leave Muon lr and momentum unchanged. Compile the bs-1024 16/24 px static shapes and warm them up in build. Decide with an off-seed run on seeds 3-10 plus one scored run, compared with E084 per added step.
ideas.expected: Time +1 to +2.5% (about 4.61-4.68 s), since the low-res phases are per-step-bound at ~2 ms per step. Placement-independent prediction: off-seed +0.05 to +0.15 pp (0.7535-0.7545). A gain >=+0.2 pp means early steps are worth more, so the next time cut should keep early bs 1024 and cut elsewhere. A gain <=0 means steps matter only late, which favours the bs-1024 tail arms. Not a tip candidate on its own, because it is slower.

The queue was empty: every earlier idea is done or dropped, so there is nothing to drop and this adds 7 new ideas. The tip is E086/E087 at about 4.565 s, with a pool of 0.7537 and an off-seed mean of 0.7530, so it has almost no accuracy margin.

**Main exploit (priority 5):** pair E084's extra-update 32 px phase at bs 1024 (+0.18 pp scored, +0.11 pp off-seed, +2.5% time) with the first fractional 32 px trim on a Muon base (3.75@32). Prediction: about -2% time at roughly tip accuracy.

**Equal-time sibling (priority 4):** keep the same number of updates but run 1.25 epochs of the 32 px phase at 28 px instead (H2.17.1). It is gated by an untimed cost measurement, and it tests H10's claim that keeping updates beats trimming them.

**Other time levers (priority 3):**
- Remove the lookahead-EMA (H6.8.1), which cuts per-step work.
- Train the whitening bias for only 0.2 epoch, decaying its LR to 0, then detach it (H2.15.2).

**Measurement and diagnostics:**
- Priority 3: calibrate the off-seed instrument (H4.2.6), with weight-checksum and cuDNN-kernel logging. Every recent verdict rests on off-seed differences of 0.18 pp or less.
- Priority 2: the E084 EMA-window confound ablation (H2.11.4), which decides whether bs 1024 is a real update-count lever.
- Priority 2: the early-vs-late update placement test (H10.1.1).

**Deliberately left out:**
- Scalar knobs, because H9 showed they have been null; this covers filter Muon lr and phase-dependent label smoothing.
- Width cuts (closed by E080).
- End-of-run averaging variants (closed by E081 and E083).
